gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the makers' runtime figures are measured at different loads, all far above what a small NAS draws: CyberPower's 9 min for the CP850PFCLCD is at half load (about 255 W), while APC quotes its Back-UPS at a 40 W 'entry-level PC'. So '850 VA gives more headroom' says nothing about minutes at a 20–40 W NAS. The only fair way to compare them is runtime at one NAS-sized load, or battery energy in Wh.
standout_why: I read holdbackup.com (cited), racksandwatts.com and techfromalex.com, and I tried the cited Synology KB page. holdbackup gives one runtime point, 66 min at 100 W for the CP1500PFCLCD, and compares nothing. racksandwatts gives no runtimes and warns against turning VA or Wh into minutes. techfromalex gives only '3-minute full-load runtime' for the CP850PFCLCD. The Synology KB page came back with no body text. None of them puts the candidates' runtimes at the same load or says how far apart the makers' reference loads are. ChatGPT's own answer sizes by VA (600–900 VA) and lists no runtime at all.
decides: This backs the small, cheap picks over the 850 VA units for a 2–4-bay NAS. The NAS only needs a few minutes on battery to get through a short blip and then shut down. The CP850PFCLCD's headline runtimes are at 255 W and 510 W, roughly 6–25× a small NAS's draw, so they don't show any advantage at NAS loads. Pure sine and price are what separate the picks, not VA. The table needs one 'minutes at 40 W' column. Each footnote should say which load the maker actually tested, and cells the maker never published should be left blank, not filled with a guess.
